newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy deputy PM says majority not in doubt.
newsitem.headline: Italy deputy PM says majority not in doubt.

text.p: Italian deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said on Friday a parliamentary commission vote against the government's 1997 minibudget did not create political problems or put its majority in doubt.

The budget commission of the lower house of parliament voted against the proposed mini-budget with 25 votes against and 24 in favour in a result which was seen as a severe embarrassment for the centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

The package will now go to the full Chamber of Deputies for a vote, where politicians say the government is likely to have to call a confidence vote on the package in order to push it through the house.
Veltroni told reporters here the vote against "doesn't create political problems and doesn't put the solidarity of the majority coalition in question."
One of two politicians who voted against the package in the commission belongs to a small socialist party which forms part of Prodi's centre-left coalition.

Veltroni said Prodi had met the socialist party's secretary that morning and the meeting had gone well. "Moreover, I know that the same socialists would vote (for the government) if a confidence vote was called."

The government has a majority in the Senate or upper house but not in the lower house where it relies on the backing of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party. Refoundation voted with the government in the commission.
